paragraphs: (2) Shammai was head of the court, and Hillel his colleague was nasi. Shammai precedes Hillel, who was nasi, because the first members of three pairs who opposed semikhah were nesi'im, and Beit Shammai agreed with them. The text therefore lists Shammai first. Since Shammai is placed first here, it counts Shammai before Hillel everywhere: Tosafot, Hagigah 16, end of a. See Hillel, whose entry attributes the precedence to humility. At first he was Hillel's pupil, then a pupil-colleague (see there). It appears he lived long like Hillel, since he is called Shammai the Elder: Kiddushin 43a, Shammai the Elder in Haggai the prophet's name. They disagreed in only three matters (see Hillel). Although irascible toward the wicked, he was humble with the righteous, and all his deeds were for Heaven's sake. All his days he ate in honor of Shabbat; from the first day of the week, for Shabbat: Beitzah 16a. So too in his dispute: he went with his staff to Yonatan ben Uzziel (Bava Batra 133b), though Yonatan was his pupil, for all Hillel's pupils were also Shammai's. They said Hillel had eighty pupils, one Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai; Avot chapter 2 says Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai received from Hillel and Shammai, since they were always together in the study house. Hillel sat submissively before Shammai like a pupil: Shabbat 17a. Tosafot, Gittin 36b, write in the Jerusalem Talmud's name: in the eighteen matters where Beit Shammai outnumbered Beit Hillel, even Elijah could not annul them, because Beit Shammai's pupils killed Beit Hillel's pupils and the decrees were maintained at the peril of lives. He prophesied to Herod when he was small that he would reign (Yuhasin, chronological section). Six matters are among Beit Shammai's leniencies and Beit Hillel's stringencies: Shabbat 77a. ‘These are matters in which Beit Hillel returned to rule like Beit Shammai’: Eduyot 1:12. Seder Rav Amram rules like Beit Shammai in six places: Tosafot, Sukkah 3a; Aguddah there; Halikhot Olam 34a. See Shemuel Ha-Nagid's Introduction to the Gemara (and see above, Beit Hillel). In the future the halakhah will follow Beit Shammai and R' Shimon ben Yohai: Vayakhel Moshe, 42b, 54a.

(3) Shammai was a reincarnation of Yehonatan and of Yehoshua bin Nun (see above, Hillel). Shammai came from Hevel's birthright side—it should read gevurah, severity—and was therefore strict, from the mystery of judgments. Because of Shammai's sin of strictness he did not accept several converts; he was therefore reincarnated as Shimon ben Azzai and did not marry. He then created converts' souls through Torah study. In this the mystery of Shammai's severity became kindness, for the awakening of converts' souls comes from Avraham's kindness. Moshe likewise did so when he separated from his wife, since he was in the mystery of kindness (Ḥesed Le-Avraham, spring 5, river 25). See above, Abaye. גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael] writes that his grave and his wife's are at Kefar Meron, on the village's ‘second side’ [כפר לצד ב׳; provisional reading], toward the upper part, in a vineyard. There is a stone full of water: when people come to pray, there is sufficient water, and the more they take, the more the water increases. If those coming to pray are wicked, they cannot bring out even one drop. Large-stone monuments stand over them (see R' Shimon ben Yohai).
(4) Avtalyon was his teacher. Bava ben Buta was his pupil. Dostai of Kefar Yatma was his pupil.
